newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police issue stern warning to opposition.
newsitem.headline: Serbian police issue stern warning to opposition.

text.p: Serbian authorities, raising the stakes in a confrontation with the opposition, issued a stern warning on Sunday to opposition leaders who have led a wave of street protests against President Slobodan Milosevic.
Belgrade police said in a statement they had been more tolerant than required and would now hold organisers and parties responsible for any protests that broke the law.
Police said recent demonstrations contained "elements of violence and serious violations of the law", the state news agency Tanjug said.
The warning follows two weeks of street demonstrations against Milosevic that have swept the capital and major towns across the country.
The protests, backed by university students, have posed an unprecedented challenge to Milosevic, who has ruled the country with an iron hand for nine years.
The demonstrations were sparked by the annulment of opposition victories in municipal polls on November 17.
The police warning and a vitriolic attack broadcast on state television against the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition signalled that Milosevic's patience was wearing thin.
A botched local election has breathed life into an ailing opposition and set off the biggest street demonstrations in five years. Milosevic crushed those protests with tanks.
The marches have been mainly peaceful except for a few days in which protesters threw stones at the state television and state newspaper offices, shattering windows.

Opposition stewards managed to put a stop to the stone throwing since Thursday and demonstrators since then have hurled eggs, fruit and red paint bombs at the two buildings -- symbols of Milosevic's authoritarian rule.
Zajedno said in a statement authorities were ready to suppress civil rights and "use police methods to put a stop to justified protests by supporters of the Zajedno coalition".
The crisis could only be solved "in a peaceful and legal manner" -- not by police, the statement said.
The police statement coincided with a condemnation of the opposition by the speaker of parliament, Dragan Tomic, who is also a member of the ruling socialist party.
Speaking on state television news, Tomic branded the Zajedno opposition coalition "fascist".
"These are not quiet demonstrations as the organisers presented them. These are destructive, massive demonstrations, with all elements of pro-fascist grouping and ideologies."
Tomic compared the Zajedno coalition with Adolf Hitler's Nazis.

"Remember when Hitler came to power, remember before he came to power, that is what he did also. Everything is being said in the name of democracy and each time violence is invoked. Belgrade is now being destroyed."
Tens of thousands took to the streets again on Sunday despite bitter cold and sleet.
The Belgrade march was smaller than previous protests due to the weather. Saturday's demonstration in the capital drew some 100,000 people.
Tensions have been mounting as the protests gained momentum but Milosevic has remained aloof.
Zajedno leaders have threatened to organise strikes in a campaign to overturn 50 years of socialist rule.
They said they planned to stage a boycott of parliament on Tuesday unless the body annuls the local elections which they accuse the socialists of rigging.
Opposition leaders said on Saturday that the coalition would form new municipal authorities this week in seven towns where they defeated the ruling socialists.
